item.title: Ball-tampering row: Pat Cummins invites media, to address 'long list and full extent' of Usman Khawaja's allegations
item.description: Australia Test captain Pat Cummins is set to respond to Usman Khawaja's allegations about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, saying he needed time to understand the claims made in the former opener's autobiography before addressing them. Khawaja's book, 'Sabr', released on Tuesday, has brought the controversy surrounding the Cape Town Test against South Africa in 2018 back into focus. In the book, Khawaja claimed that the entire Australian team knew about the plan to use sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball. He also alleged that then captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and opener Cameron Bancroft were made scapegoats by cricket administrators despite other members of the team allegedly knowing about the plan. Cummins said he would address the media on Friday at Cricket Central, where he is scheduled to train ahead of New South Wales' Sheffield Shield match. "I'm training at Cricket Central tomorrow morning before the Blues play in the Shield match," Cummins wrote on 'X'. "Happy to speak with any and all media about the events of this week at 9.30 am. I've taken some time to try and better understand the long list and full extent of Uzzy's allegations so I can respond properly." Khawaja, meanwhile, has withdrawn from interviews to promote his autobiography after facing criticism over his television interview on Tuesday evening. During the interview, he struggled to address questions about the allegations, including whether Australia's four frontline bowlers, Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon, were involved in discussions about ball-tampering. He was also directly asked whether Cummins knew about the plan to use sandpaper in advance. Khawaja declined to answer, saying he had only shared his "truth" in the book. Former Australia captain Michael Clarke has also questioned Cummins' silence on the matter, saying the team needs to establish what happened during the 2018 Test. Speaking on 2DayFM's Breakfast with Nath & Emma, Clarke expressed surprise that the current Australia captain had not yet addressed the allegations publicly. "I can't believe we haven't heard from Pat Cummins yet, the Australian captain," Clarke said. Clarke also pointed to the impact of the 2018 scandal on Australian cricket's leadership, suggesting that Cummins might not have become captain had Smith not been removed from the role following the incident.

item.title: Ten years, three kids later - Oliva back for Olympic bid
item.description: Oliva (second from left) won Commonwealth bronze for Team Wales as part of the women's team pursuit in Glasgow [Getty Images] Cyclist and mum-of-three Ciara Oliva says she has 'unfinished business' at the Olympics after making a remarkable return to the British Cycling programme. The former European champion and world bronze medallist spent almost a decade out of the sport and has three children with partner and fellow cyclist, Lewis. But after missing out on final selection to compete at the Rio 2016 Games, the 37-year-old admits she just could not give up on her Olympic dream. She returned to international competition at the summer's Commonwealth Games, winning bronze for Wales in the women's team pursuit, but says that was only the start. "I could have stopped there," she told BBC Sport Wales. "It felt like one of the most magical moments. My favourite medal I've ever had internationally, winning a bronze medal with the girls in the team pursuit in front of my children. It was like a fairytale ending in itself. "But there's unfinished business and I am going to chase my Olympic dream one last time." Horne's Rio dream inspired by scrapbook Olympic heartache fuels Oliva's comeback Oliva first joined the Great Britain cycling programme in 2014. She won bronze at the 2016 World Championships as part of the women's team pursuit. She also won two European titles in the same event. But come the Rio 2016 Olympics, Oliva was left watching on as reserve. Laura Kenny, Katie Archibald, Elinor Barker and Joanna Rowsell were chosen for the Olympic team pursuit - and they smashed the world record to take gold. "The fastest team rode," she is happy to admit. "They won gold. "But I had to stand on the sidelines and watch that happen. And I was truly heartbroken." Oliva retired in 2018 and went on to be a physiotherapist - "I honestly thought I was done". "People would mention cycling and I would discuss it, but I always found it hard to talk about the Olympics. I got so close and yet so far," she reflected. "The years went by and I had my three beautiful children, but I watched Helen Glover's documentary and I just burst into tears. I was like, I'm not done yet. "There was still that little voice that was saying, just have a crack at it one last time. "So to now have an opportunity to chase this, but this time with my family, my children by my side, watching mummy do all this crazy training day in day out, has just made the journey so much more special than I thought was even possible." Juggling training and family life Dreaming of the Olympics is one thing. Getting yourself back on a world class programme, with a baby and two pre-schoolers to look after, was a different matter entirely. At that time, less than two years ago, Oliva says she told a few close friends and family that she was considering coming out of retirement. "'Are you crazy?' was the reaction," she admited. "'Are you sure? You're sleep-deprived!' "But I think that they also know what I'm like

item.title: Orbit Global Menu: A working global menu addon for GNOME
item.description: A new extension brings a working global menu bar to the GNOME desktop, even for some apps that don’t have menu bars at all. Orbit Global Menu is a new GNOME extension that gives the GNOME desktop a feature it was intentionally designed without, and one that some users miss very badly – this vulture being one of them. It adds a working global menu bar to the GNOME top panel. We suspect this is something that will cause strongly contrasting opinions among many GNOME users: some will by puzzled why anyone would bother, while others may think "at last!" and rush to try it. There have been other attempts to do this before, and the Reg FOSS desk has tried several of them, but we never found one that worked with the majority of applications. Our fondness for this UI feature was visible in the two-part series we wrote in September on how to customize Xfce and then in part two how to get the global menu working with more apps. The problem is getting worse over time, as in recent versions (since GNOME 40 and Gtk4), the GNOME human-interface guidelines encourage smartphone-style hamburger menus, replacing the traditional horizontal menu bar. It is tricky to add global menu bar support to apps that lack a menu bar, but Orbit's developer "Unmade" found a rather labor-intensive solution. The menu bar applet contains maps of keyboard controls for 292 different apps, so it can show a menu all on its own and then send those apps simulated keystrokes to operate it. It's not the programs' full menu trees, just a subset of them, but it works. It's also not the most elegant solution, but it is a solution and it works. We tried it on Ubuntu 26.10 and every app in the full install worked to at least some extent. If you are willing and able to build and install a small additional connector, it lets the global-menu applet talk to lots more applications. The GNOME shell is unusual among open source desktop environments, to an extent that we have criticized before. GNOME Shell was designed with a distinctive look and feel of its own, unlike almost all other desktops. It has a minimalist, stripped-down layout that doesn't look or work quite like anything else, and it's intentionally not very customizable. To change how GNOME works means writing new Javascript code, then packaging it as an extension that users can install from the GNOME Extensions website. This requires both a browser extension and a "native host messaging" connector to be installed into the underlying OS – or a purpose-written app. By default, the desktop comes with neither. The end result is that GNOME lends a visual identity to the Linux desktop, one that is clear and distinct from either Windows or macOS. (Back in 2013, this vulture argued that when Microsoft threatened to sue multiple Linux vendors over infringing Windows UI patents, some 20 years ago, this UI fragmentation was just what the company wanted .) item.title: Manchester United reportedly sack Michael Carrick with Pochettino in line
item.description: Manchester United reportedly sack Michael Carrick with Pochettino in line Manchester United reportedly sack Michael Carrick as Mauricio Pochettino nears Old Trafford job Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick, according to reports, with Mauricio Pochettino expected to replace him before the Premier League trip to Liverpool on 22 November. Cameron Smith, writing for FootballTransfers , cited Fabrizio Romano and The Athletic in reporting that United had decided to dismiss Carrick with immediate effect. At the time of publication on Thursday morning, United had yet to formally announce his departure or appoint a successor. Carrick’s final fixture was a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa. A late equaliser salvaged a point at Old Trafford, but United went into the November international break in 18th place, with eight points from their opening ten league matches. IMAGO Carrick’s permanent spell falls short of his interim promise As recently as May, United had good reason to believe Carrick was the right man for the job. His work as interim manager had persuaded the club to give him the position permanently. Less than six months later, he leaves with fewer wins in all competitions this season than United managed goals in his final match. Across 15 fixtures, Carrick’s side won three, drew five and lost seven. One of those wins, against Roma in the Champions League, offered a glimpse of why his players could still command a crowd at Old Trafford. Yet European results could do nothing to improve a league position that had come to define his tenure. Bournemouth defeat put Carrick’s job in doubt The 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth in late October marked a turning point. According to FootballTransfers, Carrick was given three games to save his job. Two of the responses that followed were memorable for much the same reason: United found themselves in trouble and had enough attacking quality to recover. Against Roma, a Bruno Fernandes penalty and two goals from Matheus Cunha turned a two-goal half-time deficit into a 3-2 victory. Against Villa, United went one better in front of goal and still came away with less. Scoring four at home earned them a single Premier League point. There was evidence in those games that the players could respond to Carrick under pressure. What was missing, particularly against Villa, was the ability to put themselves in a position where a rescue act was unnecessary. Pochettino emerges ahead of Howe and Nagelsmann Pochettino, the United States head coach, has reportedly reached a verbal agreement with United. Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann, Antonio Conte and Unai Emery had also been linked with the position, but it is the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager whom FootballTransfers identifies as the expected appointment. His experience of English football would allow United to make the change without asking a new manager to learn the league during a difficult run of results. item.title: Angola celebrates 51st independence anniversary, acknowledges Nigeria’s support
item.description: The Angola Embassy in Nigeria has commended Nigeria’s support for the country’s independence, attained in 1975. Dr José Zau, Angola’s Head of Mission to Nigeria, Benin, Niger and ECOWAS, said this at the celebration of the 51st anniversary of independence on Wednesday night in Abuja. Zau described relations between the two countries as a strategic, historic and fraternal partnership, anchored in political alignment as leading African oil producers. He said Nigeria played a significant role in supporting Angola’s independence process and the consolidation of the Angolan state. “Through the Bilateral Joint Commission, the two nations have been updating and expanding dozens of agreements and memoranda of understanding. “These cover trade, transport, culture, professional training, defence and public order, cybersecurity, and academic exchange,” he said. He cited a visa-exemption agreement for holders of diplomatic and official passports, and twinning partnerships between Angolan provinces and Nigerian states, as measures to deepen ties. The twinning pairs the Namibe and Bengo provinces with the Bayelsa and Nasarawa states, he said. He said relations were strengthened by engagement between Angolan President João Lourenço and Nigerian President Bola Tinubu. Zau said the Caculo Cabaça Dam would become operational in June 2027, with the capacity to generate at least 2,172 megawatts (MW). He said the dam would raise Angola’s total capacity from 6,400 MW to about 8,600 MW. He also highlighted the country’s achievements in 2026. (NAN) The post Angola celebrates 51st independence anniversary, acknowledges Nigeria’s support appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Erdogan Urges Return To Diplomacy To End Iran-US Conflict
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Thursday said diplomacy should resume “without further delay” to end the US-Iran war after talks with his Iranian counterpart. Erdogan met Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the UN climate conference in the Turkish province of Antalya, his office said. During their discussion, Erdogan underscored “the importance of getting to the negotiating table without further delay” and said Turkey would continue to support efforts aimed at securing peace. “Common ground for agreement must be strengthened and diplomacy given a chance,” he said, expressing hope that the conflict with the US “would end as soon as possible”. The Middle East war broke out on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes that killed Iran’s supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Iran responded by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, while the militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entered the fray. Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian leaves after delivering a speech during the High-Level Segment for Heads of States and Government at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Center in Antalya on November 11, 2026. Photo by OZAN KOSE / AFP In an address to the UN climate summit on Wednesday, Pezeshkian accused the United States and Israel of inflicting severe environmental damage during attacks on the Islamic Republic. “The recent criminal and illegal aggression against Iran by America and the Zionist regime… has inflicted severe damage on the environment, releasing massive quantities of pollutants and greenhouse gases into the atmosphere,” he said. Diplomatic efforts led by Qatar and Pakistan have sought to negotiate an end to the war. Tehran wants Washington to accept a raft of demands including unfreezing assets and lifting sanctions in return for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, the vital energy conduit it has blockaded since the start of the conflict. AFP The post Erdogan Urges Return To Diplomacy To End Iran-US Conflict appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Opportunity knocked. Louisville WR TreyShun Hurry responded in big way
item.description: For the past two years, TreyShun Hurry has played two kinds of games: football games and the waiting game. After transferring from San Jose State to Louisville in 2025, the wide receiver became a starter for the Cardinals. But he was overshadowed by Chris Bell and Caullin Lacy, and limited to 122 yards and a touchdown on 15 receptions. During the offseason, UofL added Vanderbilt transfer Tre Richardson and Florida State transfer Lawayne McCoy , who were expected to be a three-headed threat with Hurry. "Last year he was playing X, he was on the backside, really didn't see the ball too much and was just trying to kind of feel his way through the season," wide receivers coach Deion Branch said about Hurry during fall camp. "He got better and better week in, week out. But now here's the opportunity for him to possibly be one of the main guys." Hurry maintained his starting position entering this season, but McCoy and Richardson became the stars of the Cards' passing offense . They were the main options, and again, Hurry waited. McCoy got hurt against Syracuse on Oct. 17 and is out indefinitely. That opened the door for Hurry to get some of those looks. It was never about Hurry's ability, only opportunity. With it, he has taken advantage. Two weeks ago, he caught his second touchdown pass as a Card. Last week at Georgia Tech, he matched his career-high with eight receptions for a 104 yards and another score. Hurry enters the Nov. 14 game at North Carolina second on the team in receptions (39) and third in yards (474). "We're missing a big piece of our offense," Hurry said of McCoy. "So I just had to step up, and so it's no drop-off for the team and stay explosive.” Hurry had seven catches for 107 yards through the first three games of the season. But over the past three games, he's had 203 yards and two touchdowns on 15 receptions. His first touchdown of the season came on a 22-yard catch from Lincoln Kienholz in Louisville's 52-24 win over Stanford on Oct. 31. Kienholz might have been just as excited as Hurry, if not more so. "I think he's a super solid receiver," the quarterback said. "He gets open when he needs to. If you go back and just look at his games, he's had multiple games with 60-plus receiving yards, which is huge. ... That's something I was driving to try to get him his first one (touchdown)." Hurry followed that performance with a career day against Georgia Tech . The California native hadn't had a 100-yard receiving game since he was with Weber State in 2023. Getting to that point required him to practice patience just as much as he practiced football. There were times when he felt discouraged, overlooked even. Kienholz tried to encourage him in those down moments, on and off the field. "Lincoln was just telling me to be patient. It's all going to come together," Hurry said. "I trust my quarterback and trust my team." He didn't complain or stop executing in practice, and he kept taking advantage of his in-game reps. He wasn't getting t

item.title: Key part of Kentucky football's passing game has yet to be unlocked
item.description: LEXINGTON — By many measures, Kentucky football 's Kenny Minchey has been among the best quarterbacks in the SEC — and the country at large — this fall. He enters this week just outside the top 10 in the FBS in completion percentage (69.9). He averages nearly 21 completions per game, which ranks third in the conference. And he's kept interceptions to a minimum, with just two all season; only Missouri's Austin Simmons has thrown more passes (283) than Minchey (266) among SEC signal callers while totaling only two INTs. But for all of Minchey's success, one reason for his efficiency is he's feasted on short throws. Per Pro Football Focus , Minchey has completed 80.8% (84 for 104) of his "short passes," which are defined of throws between 0 and 9 yards. He's even more accurate behind the line of scrimmage, where he's connected on 94.4% (67 for 71) of his screen attempts. It's a different story on longer tosses. Minchey is 24 for 42 (57.1%) on "medium passes," which are throws between 10 and 19 yards. And on deep throws — those of 20 yards or longer — he's just 11 of 31 (35.5%). Just three of his completions this season have covered 40 or more yards. For context, 15 quarterbacks nationally have at least 10 such completions, including SEC leader Arch Manning and Louisville's Lincoln Kienholz. It must be noted, of course, that the farther the throw, the higher the level of difficulty. Not to mention the fact defenders have more time to react to a ball in the air as opposed to one that doesn't even cross the line of scrimmage. His teammates haven't been perfect hauling in those aforementioned long throws, as the Wildcats are credited with two drops. (The walk-in touchdown freshman wide receiver Kenny Darby dropped at Texas A&M is the most glaring example.) Yet Minchey hasn't helped himself at times, either. Of his 31 deep throws, he has a Turnover Worthy Play Rate of 9.4%. PFF defines a Turnover Worthy Play as "a pass that has a high percentage chance to be intercepted or a poor job of taking care of the ball and fumbling." Minchey's percentage ranks 30th nationally . It's the second-worst percentage in the conference; only Arkansas' KJ Jackson has been more risky at 11.6%. The numbers don't lie: Minchey has been well-below average on deep throws. His PFF grade of 66.1 is tied for 130th of the 156 FBS quarterbacks evaluated by the site. That ranked above only two of his SEC colleagues: Auburn's Byrum Brown at 58.9 and Jackson (again) at 52.5. Stat Total SEC rank 10+ yard comp 80 T-5 20+ yard comp 28 T-4 30+ yard comp 12 T-7 40+ yard comp 3 T-11 50+ yard comp 1 T-11 Minchey's teammates have picked up the slack elsewhere, though. It should surprise no one the Cats' top two receivers in receptions and yards — Darby and tight end Willie Rodriguez — also rank 1-2 in yards after a catch (YAC). Darby has 309 yards after catches this season, while Rodriguez is at 260. No other UK player is even above 150. Bottom line: Minchey must start completing deep throws a

item.title: His days on oil rigs are done. Spence Nowinsky strikes it rich with New Mexico football
item.description: Before Spence Nowinsky built college football ’s stingiest defense, he was running through airports, inspecting storage tanks and checking gas dispensers for leaks. Football had spit him out. After a coaching change at Idaho left Nowinsky without a job, the former Minnesota State defensive lineman took work with a compliance company servicing the oil industry. The money was good. The football prospects weren’t. Then came a chance to get back in. “I think I took a $150,000 haircut to go coach football again.” CFB Unfiltered: What the CFP rankings got wrong about Indiana, Miami More than two decades later, that decision looks like one hell of an investment. Nowinsky is the architect of a New Mexico defense allowing a meager 10.89 points per game, the backbone of one of college football’s most improbable transformations under Jason Eck. The Lobos have won 17 of Eck’s first 22 games, including 14 of their past 16, and cracked the US LBM Coaches and AP polls for the first time in school history. Getting from the oil industry to Albuquerque, though, requires more than an atlas. The story traces almost 1,200 miles northeast, far closer to International Falls than New Mexico, to Mankato, Minnesota. There, at Minnesota State, the threads connecting Eck, Nowinsky and Lobos offensive coordinator Luke Schleusner began forming at different times, on different paths, before ultimately converging in Albuquerque. The plucky NCAA Division II football program is playing a disproportionate role in college football across the country this season, but especially at New Mexico, where Eck, who might be the hottest name in college football coaching circles right now, drives lowriders, fraternizes with fans as an everyman and suddenly sells out University Stadium. A former Wisconsin lineman, Eck does all of this with a modest operating budget, a different athletic director than the one who hired him two years ago and an unrelenting, uncompromising defense. Enter Nowinsky. He arrived to find one of the nation’s leakiest defenses, the No. 130 scoring unit in 2024. He helped reduce that figure to 22 points per game a year ago, then nearly halved it to claim the nation’s top spot through the first 10 weeks of this season. It’s a remarkable rise for a coach who once ran contracts for oil rigs in the nascent days of his yet-to-lift-off career and now operates college football’s stingiest defense. “It wasn’t on the patch and that type of thing, I worked for a compliance company, above ground and below ground checking storage tanks, is it leaking, are your gas dispensers in proper working condition," the barrel-chested Nowinsky says. "I literally traveled every single day, running through airports catching planes. It was ridiculous but I got an opportunity to then go back to Mankato and work." A football lifer with high school coaching roots in addition to oil-rig boots, Nowinsky now is the coordinator sticking by Eck even as larger programs inquire about his defensive services.

item.title: For Lane Kiffin to revive LSU in CFP race, Tigers need Arch Manning injection
item.description: Lane Kiffin needs an editor. LSU recently posted on the video screens in its team facility a screed hundreds of words long that epitomized why “TLDR” (Too long, didn’t read) memes exist. What it lacked in pithiness, it compensated for in corniness and included such lines as, “When you win, everybody loves you. When you lose, everybody has an opinion.” No kidding. It read like a chatbot’s attempt at an “Us Against the World” motivational ploy and lacked authenticity. To my human brain, it read more like, “Wah, wah, we keep losing, and everybody is being so mean!” Here’s what an edited version might say: Be like Arch. Three words. One necessary mentality. Basically, Kiffin needs his team to become Arch Manning. That is, do your best work after you’re counted out. Fight hardest at the darkest hour. That’s the only way LSU can rally its way into the College Football Playoff . The task starts this weekend against suddenly hot Texas. LSU requires a dose of Arch Manning philosophy Does Kiffin need Arch as his quarterback in 2027? I've heard worse ideas. In the meantime, LSU requires an injection of the resilience Manning showed after his career and Texas’ season started walking the plank in October. Say what you will about Manning — I’ve said more than I ever planned to — just don’t say this guy has an ounce of quit in him. Dare Manning to transfer, and that’s when he’ll finally prove himself worthy of being the QB1 at a school like Texas. Just a few weeks ago, Manning was a living, breathing turnover machine , and some of his teammates appeared more interested in being content creators than serious football players. The criticism extended up to the head man. I stripped Steve Sarkisian of his “Guru Club” membership card. With Texas’ season on the brink , Manning delivered the best first half of his life against Mississippi, and the Longhorns showed a spine in some tense final moments of a season-saving win. What did Manning have to say about his rise from the ashes? Well, he darn-near thanked us for cutting him down to size and serving him the world’s biggest slice of humble pie. He dined on doubt . “I’ve been hyped up all my life,” Manning said after that Ole Miss game. “I think I kind of like being disregarded and counted out.” I wanted to know more about Arch’s thinking on this, so I asked him what’s so great about being counted out. “There's something about proving people wrong,” he said with a smile. Kiffin once experienced that. He rebuilt his career, found some peace , and tasted success like never before at Ole Miss, a place where success doesn’t always come easily. Then, after his detour in the hero’s lane, Kiffin proved the naysayers right when he burned it all down for a defector’s exit to LSU. How’s that going? Well, let’s just say LSU wouldn’t need a motivational on its video screens if Kiffin’s first season was going well. item.title: Hardaway's Memphis team may offer early test for Louisville basketball
item.description: Louisville basketball agreed to a six-year series with Memphis in hopes of rekindling one of its oldest — and, at times, fiercest — rivalries. It didn't feel like one during the Cardinals' 99-73 win last December at the KFC Yum Center — their largest over the Tigers since a 95-65 beatdown Feb. 16, 1981, at Freedom Hall. Rather, it was a tale of two programs headed in opposite directions: UofL toward its first NCAA Tournament victory since 2017 and Memphis toward its worst finish in more than five decades (13-19). These aren't the same Tigers that No. 10 Louisville (2-0) will face at 1 p.m. ET Nov. 15 at FedExForum. After a 13-man roster overhaul during the offseason, coach Penny Hardaway has made quick work of restoring the positive vibes on Beale Street. Memphis is 2-1 entering the showdown against the Cards, its fourth consecutive opponent coming off a trip to March Madness this past spring. The Tigers beat then-No. 14 Iowa State 80-76 and outlasted VCU 89-88 in Week 1 before falling 105-81 at No. 19 Vanderbilt on Nov. 10. "We're going to walk into a hostile environment," coach Pat Kelsey said Nov. 7, looking forward to the matchup after UofL's win over Morehead State . "That's an unbelievable fan base there, just like Card Nation, playing in an NBA arena against a really, really high-level team." The Courier Journal caught up with The Commercial Appeal 's Memphis basketball reporter, Jason Munz , for a Q&A previewing the 92nd meeting between Louisville and the Tigers: One could make a pretty strong case for Memphis having the country's toughest opening stretch. Three games in with Penny Hardaway's 13 newcomers, what's been your biggest takeaway? Munz: The Tigers have already shown an incredible amount of resilience in a relatively short span. First, just hours before tip-off against Iowa State, they learned definitively they would be without arguably their best player, 24-year-old Serbian big man Nemanja Popovic. What do they do? Completely shift the basis of the offense and knock off a top-25 team. Then, against VCU, Memphis trailed by double digits on multiple occasions. But it never folded. Roster overhaul aside, what’s been the most notable change to Hardaway's approach in the wake of Memphis' worst season in 56 years? Munz: Honestly, for me, it simply boils down to the chemistry this team has shown thus far. You mentioned the roster overhaul — 13 new players, three of which are true freshmen. Getting that many new faces, personalities, egos to jell so quickly and so effectively couldn't have been easy. And it's not just the roster, either. Hardaway revamped his coaching staff, too, and it's all been night-and-day compared to last season. What's your score prediction for the 92nd meeting between Louisville and Memphis? Munz: I don't see Louisville losing — especially since Memphis will still be without Popovic — but I expect it to be closer than probably most think. Cardinals 88, Tigers 86. item.title: East running back Evan Garrett used family motivation to rush for 1,000 yards
item.description: Evan Garrett has a little sister who is in eighth grade. When she gets to high school, she’ll have just missed her big brother, who is a senior at Pocono Mountain East and is the starting running back for the football team. Garrett had a message for his sister before the season started: Once she gets to high school, she will see her brother’s name on the wall in the gymnasium alongside every 1,000-yard rusher in school history. After the district semifinal game, Evan’s manifestation came true. He reached the milestone as the Cardinals punched their ticket to the district championship game . “It means a lot,” Garrett said. “I got to give credit to my linemen and tight ends that block for me, but I definitely showed out and did my thing.” More: East football faces biggest challenge yet in district title game vs Southern Lehigh There were some doubts about how Garrett and the East running game would look this season with the graduation of Amari Green, the electric back who was a threat to explode for a 60, 70 or 80-yard run at a moment’s notice. It was an exciting way to play the position, which left people wondering, “What will Pocono Mountain East do now?” “I heard it plenty of times – ‘You’re never going to be like Amari. He’s gone.’ ‘East isn’t going to rush for 1,000 anytime soon,’” Garrett said. “It was all just motivation for me.” Rushing for 1,000 yards is no easy feat, so Garrett did the only thing he could: Work as hard as he could. Then work some more. Garrett said he and his teammates “went through hell” in the offseason, knowing that after the departure of so many talented seniors, he would have to step up. It showed when he played. Every yard gained was a visual example of all the squats, bench presses, deadlifts, and hills with a weighted vest Garrett did throughout the summer and fall. It felt like he truly earned every one of his 1,000 yards. “Garrett’s a guy where his average is probably between 4 and 5 yards per carry, and he’s just pounding away,” head coach Dustin Thomas said. “He runs hard every single time he gets the ball.” Even with the determination to reach his goal, Garrett did it unselfishly. With the district semifinal on the line, Thomas called a run play for Garrett, but he turned it down. Instead, he opted to lead block for his teammate and quarterback Ceejay Serfass to get the rushing touchdown. “That’s about as unselfish as somebody could be on a night where you’re chasing 1,000 yards,” Thomas said. It is the 17th time a Pocono Mountain East running back ran for 1,000 yards, and Garrett is the 15th different Cardinal to reach the milestone. But he’ll be the first name little sister recognizes when she walks in the gym next school year. This article originally appeared on Pocono Record: East running back Evan Garrett used family motivation to rush for 1,000 yards

item.title: Ohio State needs to get Jeremiah Smith more involved in final stretch
item.description: For all the impact Ohio State has gotten from wide receiver Jeremiah Smith this season, the Buckeyes have equally suffered when failing to get the ball in his hands. During Ohio State's 41-28 loss to Oregon , Smith had seven catches on nine targets, logging 133 yards and a touchdown despite going more than 28 minutes without freshman quarterback Luke Fahey throwing in his direction. "I don't think I had the numbers in front of me, but you could feel it," Ohio State coach Ryan Day said. "There was definitely conversation on the headset. There is always conversation: 'How do we get the ball to Jeremiah?' ... When you look at how we design plays, he's obviously the first thing. We're trying to make sure he's touching the ball." Ohio State ran 26 plays during a stretch in the second and third quarter stretches in which Smith had zero targets. Fahey threw 15 passes in that time, primarily to wide receiver Devin McCuin , with a 66.7% pass completion rate (10 for 15). After Smith secured his first second-half catch, the Buckeyes posted two touchdowns and 200 total yards, 87 recorded by Smith. "There are things that are designed [for Smith], and it just doesn't go that way based on what's happening, but it's always a priority," Day said. "He's had a lot of targets, but we certainly want to give him more. There's no question. And teams do a good job on how they defend him. So when those stretches come, it's everything we can do to make sure he's touching the ball." While Smith faced multi-man coverage on some occasions against Oregon, Fahey had opportunities to connect with the team-leading receiver but instead directed his throws to McCuin, who finished with nine catches on 13 targets for 84 yards. There were also plays where Smith was on the sideline, including a third down in the second quarter. Before Ohio State second-year starting quarterback Julian Sayin suffered an apparent arm injury against Indiana on Oct. 17 , Smith was considered the front-runner for the Heisman Trophy , leading the nation in most receiving categories. Smith is tied with Oregon State's Jesse Legree for a nation-leading 14 receiving touchdowns but has fallen behind several players in receptions (69) and is second to Legree in receiving yards (1,209 compared to 1,200). The performance during the 30-18 loss to USC on Oct. 31 did little to help Jeremiah Smith, as his 10 receptions resulted in only 83 yards. However, even if Smith has a game in which he is limited in yardage, getting him the ball is still a main focal point, Ohio State offensive coordinator Arthur Smith said. "That's always a focus, every week," Arthur Smith said. "He's having a historic season. Obviously, when you lose games, we'd love to have him touch the ball every play. ... So, there are things we have to do to clean up. But that's been the focal point, every week, since I've gotten here. That will never change." bmackay@dispatch.com @brimackay15 This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: Ohio

item.title: 'Entertain always:' Banana Ball entrepreneurship explained
item.description: DAYTONA BEACH − How did a pair of sports-minded entrepreneurs start a collegiate wood-bat baseball club in 2015 and turn it into a nationwide phenomenon and franchise that today is valued at between $500 million and $1 billion? Jared Orton, president of the Savannah Bananas, listed some of the ways Nov. 10 at Daytona State College: "Make baseball fun, greatest show in sports, be fan-first, entertain always, make an impact on people." Another team mantra is a reminder that while many fans have attended multiple Bananas games, for many it's their first, so it's critical for players, ticket takers and vendors in the stands to remember that it's "someone's first game." Some 450 people, including DSC students and hundreds from Volusia and Flagler schools, heard Orton explain those concepts during the L. Gale Lemerand Entrepreneurial Speaker Series in the college's Hosseini Center. The Savannah ballclub has evolved into a professional club playing in the organization it spawned, the Banana Ball Championship League − which has flipped norms and standards, such as the untimed game, on baseball's head. The Bananas are now a traveling show, playing games to sellout crowds across the country at Yankee Stadium in New York, Wrigley Field in Chicago, and even football stadiums such as Texas A&M's Kyle Field, with a capacity of 102,000. Savannah Bananas president discusses finding the right partners Orton was a student at Belmont Abbey College in Belmont, North Carolina, when he first heard about Jesse Cole, the Bananas' cofounder. "I was on the baseball team," Orton said. "Playing was a different story." Realizing he was not going to make it in Major League Baseball, Orton said he talked to his coach about people he might approach about business opportunities in the sports world, and the coach pointed him to Cole, who was running a collegiate summer-league team. Cold-calling Cole was a lesson for Orton in getting out of his comfort zone and building relationships from scratch. "I certainly wasn't great at it, but I had to get those reps in − going out and meeting people and talking about the thing he was doing," Orton said. "Those lessons are invaluable because, to me, it was let me go work for somebody, and let me be of service to them as best as I possibly can." Staying in touch with Cole led to their collaboration in Savannah starting in 2015, after the city's minor-league club, the Sand Gnats, played its final season before moving to Columbia, South Carolina. Savannah ballclub knows importance of risk-taking in order to grow Orton said of the Bananas: "The same thing has reinvented itself multiple times." Going into a marketplace like Savannah, Orton said, "We are not here to just be the next team. We are here to make baseball fun, and we tried to communicate that it was a completely different thing that we were trying to create." item.title: Honesdale Area Jaycees host 2026 basketball tournament tip-off dinner
item.description: CHERRY RIDGE — KC Pepper once again provided the backdrop for an event many local folks consider the unofficial start of the winter sports season. High school basketball coaches from across the area gathered at the popular restaurant on Monday, Nov. 9, for the 2026 Honesdale Area Jaycees Tip-Off Dinner. The celebration is held each year to announce dates and brackets for the holiday hoops tournament. This year’s event is slated for Saturday, Dec. 26, and Monday, Dec. 28, and will feature teams from Honesdale, Western Wayne, Wallenpaupack Area, Forest City and Tunkhannock. “We’re definitely excited,” chairperson Julia Parlier said. “The energy here tonight is awesome and we really appreciate how much the community comes out to support us.” More: Young sluggers flex their muscles at 47th Jaycees Home Run Derby Also by Kevin Edwards: Honesdale Area Jaycees host 2026 Wayne County Canoe Classic This marks the 66 th year the Jaycees will host their holiday basketball tournament. It’s one of the oldest in the state that features both boys and girls divisions. Honesdale is the reigning champion on the girls side, while Paupack will look to defend its boys crown when action commences in just 45 days. The first official day of winter sports practice is set for Friday, Nov. 20. Setting the stage The 2026 tourney will feature Honesdale, Wallenpaupack Area, Western Wayne and Tunkhannock in the boys bracket. Meanwhile, the Hornets, Buckhorns and Wildcats will be joined by Forest City in the girls division. Action gets underway that Saturday night with Paupack and Forest City tipping off for the initial girls game at 5:45 p.m. Next up will be Western Wayne versus Honesdale, starting at about 7:15 p.m. Boys action commences at 6:30 p.m. with Paupack battling Western Wayne. The Day One nightcap features Honesdale against Tunkhannock at approximately 8 p.m. Consolation contests and championship games will take place on Monday starting at 5:45 p.m. for the girls and 6:30 p.m. for the boys. “We can’t wait to bring our community together for this year’s tournament,” Parlier said. “We hope to see everyone there cheering on our teams for the ultimate basketball showdown.” A bit of history The Jaycees hosted their first basketball tournament in 1960. It is one of the oldest holiday athletic events in the state. In the beginning, this was a boys-only tourney and Paupack won the first two titles thanks in large part to the talents of local legend Mike Strong. Waymart then established a mini-dynasty by capturing the next four championships. The Warriors were coached by Hall of Famer Pat “Red” Walsh. Damascus won its only title in 1966, followed by St. Paul's of Scranton, Paupack (twice), Mountain View and Elk Lake. It wasn't until 1972, more than a decade after the tournament was inaugurated, that the host team copped its first crown. item.title: Sri Lanka thrash Ireland in Emerging Nations opener
item.description: Sri Lanka won by 10 wickets in Ajman [Getty Images] First T20 international, Ajman Ireland Women 105-9 (20 overs): Little 28, Hunter 21; Dilhari 3-20 Sri Lanka Women 110-0 (13 overs): Gunaratne 53*, Perera 53* Sri Lanka Women win by 10 wickets Scorecard Ireland suffered defeat in their opening Emerging Nations Trophy game in the United Arab Emirates as they lost by 10 wickets to Sri Lanka. Sri Lanka won the toss and opted to field first, with Ireland managing just 105-9 in their 20 overs. Amy Hunter, who was named vice-captain for the tournament in the absence of Orla Prendergast, was first up for Ireland and managed 21 runs, including three fours, before she was dismissed by Sathy Sandeepani. Captain Gaby Lewis exited for just four runs while Lara Maritz, making her first appearance since 2021, registered 13 before Kavisha Dilhari got her out. Louise Little was then ran out by Nilakshi de Silva after recording Ireland's highest individual total of 28. Laura Delaney added 15 runs before she exited in the same over as Little, while debutant Abi Harrison managed 13 not out to take Ireland close to a century. They did manage to edge over 100, but Cara Murray, Jane Maguire and Kia McCartney were all swiftly dismissed in the last three overs to leave Sri Lanka in a strong position. The unbeaten partnership of Vishmi Gunaratne and Hasini Perera helped them surpass the target in just 13 overs. Gunaratne registered 53 from 37 balls including six fours and one six, while Perera managed the same tally from 41 balls with eight fours and a six, as Sri Lanka claimed a comfortable victory. Lloyd Tennant's side will now turn their attention to Friday's next group game against UAE [05:00 GMT]. Ireland will also face Papua New Guinea [Monday, 16 November] and Scotland [Wednesday, 18 November] in the group stage. Get cricket news sent straight to your phone

item.title: Offensive coordinators are the latest sacrifices delivered to angry fanbases
item.description: You can practically overlay the infamous seven stages of grief atop the various stages of heartbreak that overcomes an entire football fan base when things unravel. “Shock and denial” comes first, they say, and where do we begin in confirming that one? Ohio State and probably Oregon seem to be hanging out there these days. Pain, anger and depression line up like a Murderers Row of inevitability as losses and squeak-by wins over former doormats begin to mount, and as prized recruits and key transfers turn out to be unpredictable 20-year-olds (go figure!). In the midst of it all, along comes bargaining, which always seemed more labor-intense than mere wallowing, but different strokes, you know? What form does “bargaining” take? Well, look around. At your next red-light intersection, you might be approached by a cardboard-toting man in a headset, looking for a little help until his buyout check deposits. Offensive coordinators are the current sacrifices, and predictably, not the cheap kind you’ll find at a mid-level, off-broadway conference cellar-dweller. Jason Beck (Michigan) and Dana Holgorsen (Nebraska) are the latest to be jettisoned. Earlier, it was Drew Mehringer (Oregon) and Ben Arbuckle (Oklahoma). Presidents dump cabinet members, candidates fire campaign managers, CEOs spin the wheel and find a lower C-suite lamb to offer the unhappy masses. Head coaches on heated seats fire coordinators. At Florida (Buster Faulkner) and Ohio State (Arthur Smith), big-money coordinators are under fire just two-thirds of the way through their first seasons on the job. "Am I asking for Arthur Smith to be fired right now? Not necessarily. Just have Ryan be more involved in the offense." 🌰📉 @MattFontana83 and @jzwick12 break down whether Ryan Day needs to take back play-calling duties and how this team plans to pick up the pieces. 👇 pic.twitter.com/B1mHg2ELGI — Locked on Buckeyes (@LOBuckeyes) November 10, 2026 Some defensive coordinators were also cast aside this week: Kevin Kane (Purdue) and Jason Semore ( Georgia Tech ). While Smith remains on the job at Ohio State, Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day has been under pressure to do something/anything to temper the flaring disgust. The Buckeyes have already lost three games, something they hadn’t done in 15 years. Maybe it’s all that success that allowed Day, for now, to simply unload special-teams coach Robby Discher. All of this is cheaper than buying out the head coach, of course. And probably smarter in most cases. All in all, in its own way, it all points to one unmistakable trait of this new age of college ball. When you have to piece together, or even slap together, a new roster every spring, it’s built in large part without the cohesion gathered by two, three or four years of familiarity. There’s no way to know what you have until late November closes in and no one’s in the mood to give leeway, much less thanks. item.title: Germany boss confident Musiala will return to his best despite Hoeneß doubts
item.description: Germany boss confident Musiala will return to his best despite Hoeneß doubts Germany sporting director Rudi Völler has backed Jamal Musiala to return to top form following a series of setbacks for the Bayern Munich midfielder in recent years. Musiala missed the start of the season after suffering on-field collapses linked to a neurological condition. Upon his return, he then sustained a muscle fibre tear that has kept him sidelined for more than a month. Nevertheless, Völler has no doubts that the 23-year-old will bounce back and rediscover his best form. "Based on the information I have, I am convinced that he will come back as strong as he was before the injury. There is no reason to be sceptical about that. I am absolutely convinced that we will see Jamal Musiala in outstanding form at many, many tournaments – he is still very young, after all," Völler said on DAZN's “Never Talk Alone” programme. This season's concerns follow a horrific fibula fracture Musiala suffered after colliding with Gianluigi Donnarumma during Bayern Munich's Club World Cup quarter-final against Paris Saint-Germain in the summer of 2025. The injury kept him out of action for several months. "Unfortunately, he was also unlucky back then with Donnarumma, when he suffered a serious ankle injury and had to undergo surgery. It really was a very, very serious injury. He needs some time to get back to where he was. And if he can avoid further problems like that, I am completely optimistic that he will be able to produce top-level performances again," Völler said. Regarding Musiala's neurological condition, Völler said he would be more concerned about recurring muscle injuries. “It's not something you see every day in professional sport, but I actually thought it was a good thing that it became public and that it's being handled sensibly," he said. Bayern supervisory board member Uli Hoeneß recently described Musiala's situation as a dilemma for the club, raising doubts over whether the midfielder will ever return to his previous level. "Just imagine if Bayern Munich were now to question his contract and say: What he is capable of delivering now is no longer what is stipulated in the contract," Hoeneß told BR. Völler, however, doesn't think too much should be read into Hoeneß's comments. “I don't see it as that dramatic. These are just things – we all know Uli. Perhaps he also likes to provoke people a little in his own way. But he never really means any harm. That has always been one of his great strengths, even over all these decades: he goes out of his way to protect his own players and support them,” he said. "With one player, he might be particularly complimentary; with another, he might be a little more critical. But fundamentally, he loves them all."

item.title: St. Charles edges defending champion Jerome in boys soccer state semi
item.description: St. Charles’ biggest adjustment at halftime of a Division I boys soccer state semifinal was clogging the middle and making Dublin Jerome work on the perimeter of the field. As luck – or strategy – would have it, St. Charles ended up scoring the game’s only goal through traffic in the middle. Cardinals senior forward Sam Lofthouse punched in a shot amid a scrum in front of the net with 10:48 to play in the second half Nov. 11 at Olentangy, and a stifling defense held off the defending Division I state champions from there in a 1-0 win that put St. Charles into its second state final in four seasons. “I saw my outside back [junior Tyler Bushong] dribbling down, he crossed it in and I made a one-touch finish to the bottom corner,” Lofthouse said. “We have been talking about just putting it on frame. That’s all you can do and let the rest take care of itself.” Playing in its fourth consecutive state tournament, St. Charles (18-3-1) will face Kettering Fairmont (14-5-3) in the championship game at 7 p.m. Nov. 15 at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field. Fairmont reached its first final with a 2-1 win over Strongsville at Westerville Central. Lofthouse shifted to defense after he scored, helping St. Charles win a showdown in which it was outshot 10-7 and saw Jerome (18-3-1) put together its final serious charge with about 5 minutes left. “We decided to clog up the middle because they didn’t have many people outside,” Cardinals senior defender Tyler Stoner said. “So it would slow down the process if we had more people inside. We would have to make them change their identity and go through a different path to try to score.” Sophomore goalie Eli Wichlinski made seven saves for St. Charles, which tangled with the Ohio High School Athletic Association in September and October to play in Division I after originally being assigned to Division II. Sophomore goalie Micah Neil made three saves for Jerome. “They had more chances than us … hats off to everything they did,” St. Charles coach Chris Vonau said. “I am just super proud. We have been using the ‘climb the mountain’ slogan with everything we have been through. I am speechless, and I am never speechless about how proud I am of my guys. We made some adjustments [and] the guys bought in. They were better than us in the first half, so we had to make a move.” The Cardinals will be one of four central Ohio teams playing for state championships Nov. 15 and 16, joining CCL rival Watterson (Division III), Worthington Christian (Division IV) and Fairbanks (Division V). Watterson and Worthington Christian are seeking title repeats. Worthington Christian puts clamps on West M, eyeing another crown In Division IV, the veteran Warriors never took their collective feet off the accelerator in their semifinal against Zanesville West Muskingum, scoring twice in each half to back a lock-down defensive effort in a 4-0 win at Granville's Walter Hodges Stadium. Worthington Christian (18-3-2) advanced to the final against Cincinnati Wyoming

item.title: Dan Campbell vs Mike Vrabel: A look back at when they faced off as players
item.description: When the Detroit Lions take on the New England Patriots in Germany on Sunday, Nov. 15, it will be a head-to-head matchup of former players for their respective teams. And about 20 years ago, they went head-to-head on the field. Let's take a little walk down memory lane, back to Dec. 3, 2006, when the 2-9 Lions traveled to face the 9-2 Patriots looking to play spoilers down the stretch. They were surprisingly in the game late into the fourth quarter and had the ball with a 21-all tie and about 8:30 to go in the game. That's when Dan Campbell, playing tight end in those days, made his lone catch of the day, a 21-yard down the seam. He popped up and showed off that trademark Campbell energy with a boisterous fist pump. On the next play, though, Mike Vrabel picked off Lions quarterback Jon Kitna. It proved costly, as the Patriots survived, 28-21. The play before Vrabel's INT, Dan Campbell caught a 21-yard pass on him, despite Vrabel re-routing him up the seam. It was Campbell's only catch that day. The Pats won 28-21. https://t.co/XAe2gC4Dj0 pic.twitter.com/OIR6Li7VXk — Andrew Callahan (@_AndrewCallahan) November 11, 2026 Campbell and Vrabel won't be thumping shoulder pads in this one, but they'll still face off in a game that's important to both teams. The Lions, of course, are trying to keep pace in the highly competitive NFC North at 6-2, while the Patriots are in danger of seeing their season spiral after a shellacking from the Green Bay Packers sent them to 5-4. This article originally appeared on Detroit Free Press: Dan Campbell vs Mike Vrabel: A look back at when they faced off as players

item.title: 2027: APC Is Working Towards Coronation, Not Election, ADC Ologbondiyan On Court Voiding Atiku’s Candidacy
item.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has described the court’s voidance of its principal presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, as an attempt to silence the voices of opposition parties, alleging that the ruling party, the All Progressives Congress (APC), was working to present its candidate, Bola Tinubu, as the sole candidate in the coming 2027 general elections. Justice Lifu, on November 5, nullified the David Mark-led leadership of the ADC and declared invalid the actions taken by the caretaker committee. The ruling followed a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the party, who challenged the process through which Mark and other members of the committee assumed leadership after the resignation of former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu. The court’s decision was reported to have affected the process that produced Atiku as the party’s presidential candidate, as the Mark-led committee organised the primary election. The ADC, however, rejected the judgment, describing it as legally indefensible and accusing the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of seeking to weaken the opposition. The party also said it would challenge the decision, citing an earlier judgment by Justice Musa Liman of the same Federal High Court, which it said had affirmed the legitimacy of the Mark-led leadership. A combo of NDC Lawyer, Kalu Kalu, and Atiku Abubakar. Speaking further on ADC’s standpoint on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Thursday, Kola Ologbondiyan, Spokesperson of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, accused the APC of working toward coronating Tinubu in 2027 instead of allowing for healthy competition. Ologbondiyan alleged that the APC has given no room for opposition politics. “So it now goes into what we have been saying because what we now want is that no candidate must stand against during the election, and that goes to nothing as far as we are concerned in the African Democratic Congress.” The NDC’s Spokesperson said that his party has taken the necessary steps to appeal the judgement. “We are sure that we will go to the next level in the administration of justice; we believe that all this manipulation and attempt to suppress Nigerians, all this move to dismantle democratic structures will not work. We have seen it over and over again; it will not stand.” He alleged that the APC is working to ensure that the ADC candidate, Abubakar, is not on the ballot for the 2027 election, and to enthrone President Tinubu as a life president. “I want Nigerians to know, anyone thinking that this is about ADC is not reading the processes well. item.title: Why FAMU football has a score to settle with Mississippi Valley State
item.description: Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, has been circled on the calendar since Florida A&M released its 2026 football schedule. The Rattlers are seeking retribution on a team that has unexpectedly defeated it the last two seasons, Mississippi Valley State. “There is a little bit of an added motivation when it comes down to it,” said first-year FAMU head coach Quinn Fordham Gray Sr. “This team has done a good job of having our number over the last two years.” Since taking an all-time 6-0 lead over the Delta Devils, FAMU has been stunned in defeat two years in a row. The previously unheard-of wins surprised college football fans, as Valley had long been one of the Southwestern Athletic Conference’s punching bags. In November 2024, a 24-21 triumph by Mississippi Valley snapped FAMU’s sacred 23-game home winning streak on Ken Riley Field at Bragg Memorial Stadium . It spanned five seasons and was the second-longest active streak in the NCAA Division I Football Championship Subdivision. Beating FAMU was the Delta Devils only win that year and their first victory in 15 games, a losing streak dating back to the previous season. Then, in 2025, FAMU made a post-Thanksgiving trip to Itta Bena after Atlanta’s Georgia Football Classic neutral-site game was canceled due to promoter issues and was rescheduled as a normal home SWAC game. Mississippi Valley won once again 35-31. It was the final blow as FAMU decided to move on from second-year head coach James Colzie III days later . “Just understanding what they did to us in ’24, then obviously last year,” FAMU redshirt senior running back Jamal Hailey told the Tallahassee Democrat. “We got some revenge on our hearts still.” A team that was once viewed as a bye week across the SWAC now comes as a formidable opponent for the Rattlers. Early in the season, the Delta Devils pulled off an upset over current SWAC West leader Prairie View A&M, 28-27, and also beat league opponent Texas Southern 38-34. This isn’t the ‘Same old Valley,’ led by second-year head coach Terrell Buckley, a former Florida State Seminoles star returning to Tallahassee this weekend. Conversely, MVSU has an NCAA Division II loss to Delta State this year, 21-6. FAMU doesn’t know which Mississippi Valley will show up. But the goal remains the same — end a losing streak that has since cast a dark cloud over the program, as FAMU has gone 8-16 since that shocking November 2024 afternoon in Tallahassee. “They don’t lose to Valley,” said FAMU freshman quarterback Armond Parker . “Since it happened in the past two years, we got to change it.” The Week 11 FAMU-MVSU game kicks off at 3 p.m. on SWAC TV and 96.1 JAMZ . It is Senior Day for the Rattlers. It'll be a shot for the Rattlers to end an overall four-game losing streak this year, a current four-game skid at home, and to get payback on who sent FAMU team on its ongoing downward spiral nearly two years ago. FAMU (2-8, 1-5 in SWAC) and Valley (3-7, 2-4 in SWAC) are also fighting not to finish last in the SWAC East,

item.title: Cuonzo Martin says Bears are 'done auditioning,' ready for Division-I slate
item.description: SPRINGFIELD — Missouri State men’s basketball has its sights set on next week after the Bears (3-0) defeated Division-II Newman 89-62 on Tuesday, Nov. 10. This was the Bears’ third victory over a Division-II opponent this season. Missouri State defeated Lincoln and Truman State by at least 17 points each last week. “No disrespect to the three opponents that we’ve played, but we’re done auditioning,” Missouri state coach Cuonzo Martin said. “Now we in it.” Missouri State: Lady Bears find defensive rhythm early behind transfer Hannah Linthacum Missouri State men's basketball: Meet the revamped roster Missouri State will host Abilene Christian for its first game against a Division-I opponent on Monday, Nov. 16. Here’s what we can expect from Missouri State’s new-look roster. Williams, Acimovic to lead the offense Entering the season, it was no surprise that guard Trey Williams Jr. would lead the offense. The main question was who would join him. Bosnian center Andrej Acimovic has been filling up the stat sheet. The Indiana transfer was named Conference USA’s Player of the Week after scoring 24 points against Lincoln and adding 31 points versus Truman State. Against Newman, the Jets doubled Acimovic every time that he touched the ball. It gave Williams even more time to operate. He scored a career-high 26 points on 9-for-17 shooting. “I knew I was going to have to step up and score more (against Newman),” Williams said. “We have some things that we still need to get better at.” Williams and Acimovic’s one-two punch is something to watch as the season goes along. The chemistry the duo has in pick-and-rolls, along with transition buckets, has been smooth early on. Block parties to be expected Against Newman, Missouri State finished with 16 blocks, a new-program record. Newcomer Ngundeng Ruey tied a Missouri State record with seven blocks. The Bears have finished with double-digit blocked shots in every game this season. “We are tall, long and we can move,” Ruey said. “Whenever I have a game like this, it’s a block party and everyone is doing their job.” It was a point of emphasis for Martin to recruit longer and more athletic players. The team’s activity around the rim has been obvious through the first set of games. This year’s team has 10 players at 6-foot-7 or taller. This is the tallest Missouri State team since 2006, when Missouri State athletics were first tracking rosters online. It’s safe to assume that this is the tallest Bears roster in program history. The closest was the 2021 team, which featured seven players who were 6-foot-7 or taller. “I think very valuable," Martin said about his team’s shot-blocking ability. “Congratulations to the guys on blocking those shots. You see it a lot in practice." Melakih Cunningham to be spark plug off the bench Sophomore guard Melakih Cunningham has enjoyed a big start to the new season. item.title: Tanuki: Pon’s Summer review – an adorable raccoon mends the world, one parcel at a time
item.description: Nintendo Switch/2, PlayStation 4/5, Xbox One/series X/S, PC; Denkiworks/Inpleron Limited This gentle game of fixing and fetching, in which you play as a furry post office worker on a BMX, has a slow, calming magic that delights in routine and restoration Arriving alongside November’s blue wave , Tanuki: Pon’s Summer is a game of quiet restoration that feels perfectly suited to the current moment. Tasked with repairing an ancient shrine in the weeks leading up to a local festival, you’ll find yourself cleaning out trash, mending broken arches and slowly bringing a small rural community back together. It sounds a bit like JL Carr’s compact but enchanting novel A Month in the Country , except instead of shell-shocked veterans of the first world war you’re left exploring the rich inner life of a Japanese racoon dog who can ride a BMX. Even so, the mixture of steady progress and general low stakes proves intoxicating. This is a short game, but it’s hard not to linger over it. Continue reading...

item.title: Floyd Mayweather To Launch Tmt Frontrow Fight Series In Nigeria
item.description: ABUJA, NIGERIA – 11 November 2026 – Boxing legend Floyd “Money” Mayweather will arrive in Abuja on Thursday, 12 November, to announce the launch of the TMT Frontrow Fight Series Nigeria and explore investment opportunities in Nigeria’s mining and solid minerals sector. The initiative aims to identify, train and promote young Nigerian boxing talent through the Frontrow Fight Series boxing academies and grassroots development programmes across Lagos, Abuja, Enugu, Calabar and other locations. The first TMT Frontrow Fight Series event is planned for 2027, with Floyd Mayweather also fighting in Nigeria during the same year. ABUJA PRESS CONFERENCE Mayweather will address the media in Abuja on Friday, 13 November 2026, to outline the Frontrow Fight Series and its plans to develop and empower Nigerian youth through boxing. BANGKOK FIGHT – 19 DECEMBER 2026 Mayweather will also discuss his upcoming fight in Bangkok, Thailand, against Australian light heavyweight boxer Matt “The Jedi” Floyd, who has a professional record of 15 wins from 17 fights. Further details of the fight, including how Nigerian boxing fans can subscribe to watch the event, will be announced at the Abuja press conference. item.title: Travelling to the UAE from Nigeria in 2027? Here’s What You Should Know About Tourist Visas Before You Fly
item.description: Planning a trip to Dubai in 2027? You are not alone. Every year, more and more travellers add the UAE to their holiday list. Some go for the beaches, some for the shopping, and others just want to see the famous Burj Khalifa up close. But before you book your flight, there is one important thing to take care of first, your visa. The good news is that getting a UAE tourist visa is easier than it used to be. Most of the process happens online, and your visa comes straight to your email. Still, the rules are not the same for every traveller. Some people get a visa on arrival, while others must apply before they fly. A few small mistakes can also slow things down or even get your application rejected. So let us walk through what you really need to know before you pack your bags. Do Nigerian Travellers Need a Visa for the UAE? Yes, Nigerian travellers need a visa to enter the United Arab Emirates for tourism. The UAE lets travellers from some countries enter without a visa, or get one when they land. But Nigeria is not on that list. If you hold a Nigerian passport, you must apply for your UAE tourist visa before you fly. That means you cannot just show up at Dubai International Airport and sort things out there. Your visa must be approved and in your inbox before you check in for your flight. The process is not hard, though. With the right documents and a trusted service, most people get through it without any stress. Whether this is your first trip or your fifth, this guide will help you from start to finish. UAE Tourist Visa Types: Picking the Right One for Your Trip The UAE offers a few tourist visa options. The right one for you depends on how long you plan to stay and how often you want to come and go. Here are the most common choices: Visa Type Best For 14-day visa Short trips, stopovers, quick city breaks 30-day visa Regular holidays, medium-length stays 60-day visa Longer vacations, family visits, extended stays Each visa comes with its own rules. Some let you enter only once. Others let you come and go many times. The validity period also changes from one visa to another. For example, a visa might be valid for 60 days, but it may only let you stay for 30 days inside the country. Always read the details before you book your flight. How the Application Process Actually Works Applying for a UAE tourist visa in 2027 is almost all digital. You no longer need to post papers or wait in long embassy lines. Online platforms like VisaTop.com have made the whole thing easier. You can now apply from your home, your office, or even your phone. The process usually has three simple steps. Step 1: Gather Your Documents At a minimum, you will need: A clear scanned copy of your passport (valid for at least six months beyond your travel dates) A recent passport-sized photo that meets the rules You may also be asked for: Hotel booking confirmation Return flight tickets Bank statements or proof of funds Travel insurance details Step 2: Submit and Pay Once your pa

item.title: Indonesian Vice President Resigns In High School Diploma Scandal
item.description: Indonesia’s vice president resigned Thursday, undone by a scandal over his high school diploma that has added to pressure on a government facing widespread dissatisfaction over the economy, graft and wildfires. There had been repeated calls for Gibran Rakabuming Raka, 39, to step down following a Supreme Court ruling last month to annul his high school qualification, obtained abroad. On Thursday, he submitted his resignation to President Prabowo Subianto and to parliament. Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka (C) arrives at the vice president’s palace after submitting his resignation letter to the People’s Consultative Assembly in Jakarta on November 12, 2026. Photo by ABIMANYU / AFP Prabowo told reporters he had accepted Gibran’s resignation “with a heavy heart” and praised him for acting “for a greater cause, for the interests of the nation, the state, and the people of Indonesia”. “He certainly feels that he has pursued his education through an orderly process, but we all understand that the education system abroad is different from the education system in Indonesia,” the president said. Indonesia’s vice president does not have many constitutionally defined powers apart from acting as the president’s representative at official events and taking over if his boss is incapacitated. ‘Political realignment’ Gibran’s downfall came after thousands of Indonesians took to the streets in recent weeks to protest economic hardship, graft, perceived authoritarianism and the government’s handling of months of devastating wildfires emitting toxic haze. University students protest demanding a government review including lowering the prices of basic commodities, military involvement in civilian affairs, free meal program, taxation of sanitary pads and addressing the issue of wildfires in Surabaya on November 10, 2026. (Photo by Juni KRISWANTO / AFP) | Juni KRISWANTO / AFP His exit is likely to complicate a loose governing alliance that includes the parties of Prabowo and of his predecessor Joko Widodo — Gibran’s father, who goes by Jokowi. The resignation “marks a significant political realignment, but does not necessarily threaten government stability”, according to Khairul Fahmi, executive director of the Institute for Security and Strategic Studies (ISESS) think tank. “Jokowi will retain political influence, but Gibran’s departure could reduce his network’s direct access to power. For Prabowo, this creates greater room to consolidate his leadership and pursue his own political agenda,” Khairul told AFP. Two years into his term, Prabowo’s popularity has reached record lows. Last week, Indonesian authorities arrested the former national police chief and three senior police officials for allegedly tapping the president’s telephone. On Thursday, police said they were investigating possible treason. Prabowo’s rise to power was widely credited to support from the popular Jokowi, who served two terms from 2014 to 2024. item.title: London hotel put admin login for booking website on whiteboard behind the front desk
item.description: Welcome, once again, to PWNED, where all the victims are self-owned. This week, we welcome you to a London hotel where you could check out its admin credentials for a booking website just by walking past the front desk. Our story comes courtesy of Neycho Tepavicharov, co-founder of Flashcloud, a Delaware-based web hosting company. He was staying at a hotel in London when he noticed a shocking breach of basic security protocols by management, who were a little too hospitable with their credentials. As he was passing through the lobby, Tepavicharov noticed that the door behind the front desk was open and, inside that back room, there was a whiteboard. On the whiteboard, written in plain English, were the hotel’s Booking.com administrative username and password. Anyone near the desk could clearly see the login information, and if they didn’t have time to write it down, they could have snapped a picture for later use. As Tepavicharov explains, there’s plenty of mischief you could perform with these credentials. “With that login, someone could change or cancel reservations, see guests’ names and contact details, or message guests pretending to be the hotel,” he said. “Fake 'please confirm your payment' messages sent from compromised hotel accounts are a well-known scam.” An attacker could potentially exploit that access to disrupt hotel operations or target guests with convincing scams. Whether the exposed credentials alone would have been enough to access the account would depend on its security settings. Tepavicharov decided to play the role of good samaritan and warn the hotel’s manager that the business was endangering itself by showing everyone its password. “I asked to speak with the manager and showed him what I’d seen. He was mortified and very grateful,” Tepavicharov said. “Nobody on staff had thought of it as a risk. It was just the easiest way for the whole team to share one login.” After Tepavicharov talked to the manager, not only did the hotel change its ways, but it also moved its website to his hosting service, Flashcloud. Tepavicharov notes that there are plenty of takeaways from this incident. Most important: give each user dedicated credentials with their own separate login, and use multi-factor authentication. “The lesson is an old one, but it keeps happening,” he said. “Shared logins end up written somewhere convenient. Give each staff member their own login, turn on two-factor authentication, and keep passwords in a password manager, not on the wall.” ®

item.title: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang: US media
item.description: Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, US media reported Wednesday, as the chip giant’s chief faces new accusations of infidelity, after revelations he had an affair with a woman accused of spying for China. The tech company’s board was preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang’s future, according to the Wall Street Journal, which quoted people familiar with the matter. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang was also involved in a second extramarital affair, with a subordinate, saying there was video evidence of the 63-year-old executive being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. Powell, 48, has been a public face of Nvidia’s efforts to expand the chip technology into higher education and health care, and was speaking at a San Jose, California conference where they “were seen being affectionate at the hotel” by bystanders, the Times reported. The report of the second affair follows Huang’s acknowledgment of a relationship with Alice Huang, a senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The Wall Street Journal reported that the two were photographed together in Taipei in 2024 and 2025. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this past spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. The Nvidia CEO admitted to having had a relationship with Huang — to whom he bears no familial relation — in a note to Nvidia employees Sunday, writing: “I was unfaithful to my wife.” The same day Nvidia’s board of directors said in a statement that they’d launched “an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” “I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company,” Huang wrote in his statement. He has also been called on by Congress to provide a closed-door briefing on his interactions with Alice Huang, the Times reported. As the artificial intelligence industry surge has spurred Nvidia’s stock prices to new heights, Huang has appeared at US President Donald Trump’s side at White House events, as recently as last month when he accepted a National Medal of Science from the Republican leader. Huang was among the world’s most influential tech leaders — including Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos and Mark Zuckerberg — who vowed to self-regulate AI against possible threats, as Trump rejected calls for government oversight and dismissed warnings the technology could wipe out humanity. Nvidia shareholders filed a class action lawsuit against Huang and the AI chip maker for failing to disclose information about the relationship to investors. Nvidia shares have plummeted in recent days since Huang admitted to the affair.
